flag.note: Organic sales grew 4% in the September quarter and guidance was kept; reported cash $15.4B against debt $38.9B, not near the trigger.
Third-quarter gross dollar volume rose 7% and purchase volume 9%; no sign of shrinking volume or share loss to a rival rail.
No large Lockheed program cancelled; a small Navy decoy program was cut in budget papers, and a weak-source report says F-35 orders may be halved.
Q3 net income up 16% and debt fell $1.5B in the quarter; Norfolk Southern merger funding is not yet described and could add debt later.
flag.source: Union Pacific Q3 2026 results (Business Wire via Finviz)

flag.note: Q3 free cash flow was $12.0B versus $4.9B a year ago and the $1.78 quarterly dividend was declared; no sign oil is too low.
Q3 rated issuance fell 2% to about $1.7 trillion, still second-highest for a third quarter; management expects a big Q4 drop against a high base.
Revenue up 7%, year-to-date free cash flow $11.4B, and full-year cash flow guidance was raised; I did not find a debt figure, so debt is not confirmed.
J&J proposed a talc settlement of up to $5.5B, with up to $3B paid in 2027; it had already reserved $11B, so new debt is not shown.
Backlog hit a record $63.7B at Sept. 30, up $10B from June 30; the two-quarter shrink has not happened.
